# authwise_guard_cluster_trust (Resource)

A Kubernetes cluster registered on a Guard network: its pods may join the network with their own projected service account token, under the trust's rules (`authwise_guard_cluster_trust_rule`). No secret is stored or handed out. The cluster mints the token for the network's `audience`, it lives minutes, and guard-control checks it against the cluster's signing keys.

The keys come from one of two places. `discover = true` reads the issuer's OIDC discovery document and keys, and reads them again as they rotate: GKE, EKS and AKS publish theirs. `jwks` uploads the keys, for a cluster whose issuer guard-control cannot reach (k3s, RKE2, kubeadm: `kubectl get --raw /openid/v1/jwks`). The upload is the keys until it is replaced, so when the cluster rotates its keys, change `jwks` and apply.

This is how a cluster's trust is declared: the Guard operator in the cluster holds no Guard administrative credential.

A trust is never deleted. **Destroy revokes it**: no pod joins through it again, and the nodes that joined stay until they are removed. A trust revoked out of band drops out of state at refresh, and the next apply registers the cluster again as a new trust. `issuer` never changes: a different issuer is a different cluster.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A GKE cluster, whose issuer guard-control reads.
resource "authwise_guard_cluster_trust" "gfk" {
  tenant_id    = "t-01"
  network_id   = authwise_guard_network.office.guard_network_id
  display_name = "gfk-nonprod-uc1"
  issuer       = "https://container.googleapis.com/v1/projects/acme-nonprod/locations/us-central1-a/clusters/gfk-nonprod-uc1"
  discover     = true
}

# An on-premises cluster whose issuer guard-control cannot reach: its keys
# are uploaded, from `kubectl get --raw /openid/v1/jwks > ops-jwks.json`.
# When the cluster rotates its keys, refresh the file and apply.
resource "authwise_guard_cluster_trust" "ops" {
  tenant_id    = "t-01"
  network_id   = authwise_guard_network.office.guard_network_id
  display_name = "ops-rke2"
  issuer       = "https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local"
  jwks         = file("${path.module}/ops-jwks.json")
}

# The audience the Guard operator in the cluster sets on the token it
# projects.
output "gfk_audience" {
  value = authwise_guard_cluster_trust.gfk.audience
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `display_name` (String) Unique in the network, at most 64 characters.
- `issuer` (String) The cluster's service account issuer, exactly as its tokens carry it in `iss` (`kubectl get --raw /.well-known/openid-configuration`). With `discover` it must be an https URL whose host resolves to a public address. Changing it replaces the resource: the old trust is revoked and a new one registered.
- `network_id` (String) The network's id, `authwise_guard_network.<name>.guard_network_id`. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `tenant_id` (String) The kit tenant's id (`t-…`) the Guard row belongs to. Guard has no tenant of its own since the tenant collapse (tf#65). The provider's `tenant_id` is not used. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `description` (String)
- `discover` (Boolean) `true` to read the issuer's discovery document and its keys. Give this or `jwks`.
- `jwks` (String) The cluster's JWKS document, as JSON: at most 64 KiB and 16 keys, each RSA of 2048 bits or more or EC P-256. Give this or `discover`. guard-control never returns it: `key_ids` says which keys it holds. After an import it is unknown to Terraform, so the next apply uploads the configured document again.

### Read-Only

- `audience` (String) The audience a joining pod's projected token must carry, `guard:tenants/t-…/networks/n-…`: the same for every trust of the network. The Guard operator sets it on the token it projects.
- `created_at` (String)
- `created_by` (String)
- `guard_cluster_trust_id` (String) The trust's id, `ct-…`: a rule's `cluster_trust_id`.
- `key_ids` (List of String) The `kid` of each key in use.
- `keys_error` (String) Why the last read of the keys failed; null when it worked.
- `keys_updated_at` (String) When the keys were last read or uploaded, RFC 3339.
- `last_join_at` (String) When a pod last joined through the trust, RFC 3339.
- `name` (String) The trust's full name, `tenants/t-…/networks/n-…/clusterTrusts/ct-…`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the trust's full name. An uploaded jwks is never read back, so
# the first apply after an import uploads the configured document again.
terraform import authwise_guard_cluster_trust.gfk tenants/t-01/networks/n-01/clusterTrusts/ct-01
```
